@casarthakahuja #02
Sarthak Ahuja on Instagram: "If you have a bank loan currently, you immediately need to take this one step as your next EMI is going to be higher... The RBI increased the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.5%, which means by 0.25%.... So if your floating home loan was earlier at 7.5%... it will now be at 7.75%... This means, you either have the choice to increase your EMI outflow per month to keep the same tenure, or increase the tenure to keep the EMI the same... Most banks will silently increase your tenure... because they make more money by doing it... I’ll explain the math... Imagine you had a loan of Rs 1 crore for 20 years at 7.5%... your EMI would be Rs ~80,559/-... and you would pay a total interest of Rs 93 lakh on your loan... When the rate changes to 7.75% and the duration continues to be 20 years, your EMI goes up by only Rs 1500 per month, and your total interest payout is Rs 97 lakhs... But if you keep your EMI the same to Rs ~80,500 and increase duration to 1 year... you end up paying an interest of Rs ~1,03,000/-... almost Rs 6 lakhs higher. So take the option of paying Rs 1500 extra as EMI per month instead of increasing the tenure. #casarthakahuja"

@tim.spector #12
Tim Spector MSC FRCP MD FRSB OBE on Instagram: "Did you know your gut and brain are connected by a nerve that runs between them? It’s called the vagus nerve, and it’s one of the main communication routes between your gut and your brain. What’s fascinating is that this communication goes both ways. Your brain constantly sends signals to your gut, and your gut also sends signals back to your brain. And your gut microbes are part of this complex conversation too. This helps explain some things we’ve all experienced. Why can stress upset your stomach? Why does your mood affect your digestion? And why might what happens in your gut influence how you feel? Scientists are still learning exactly how all of these connections work, but the gut-brain axis is absolutely fascinating to me. It’s one of the reasons I wrote Good Mood Food. I wanted to take the latest research on the connection between food, the gut, and the brain and bring it into the kitchen with simple, comforting recipes that make it enjoyable to nourish your gut and brain and support your overall health. Good Mood Food is out on 22 October and available to pre-order now. You can find the link in my bio. Let me know if there’s a topic you’d like me to talk more about next."

@alliekmiller #22
Allie K. Miller - AI/ML • Tech on Instagram: "One of the hardest parts of running AI agents has turned out to be deciding when they should interrupt you. If they check in too often, you've built a very expensive notification system. If they check in too rarely, you find out Thursday about something that went out Tuesday. So start by sorting the work by one question: how bad is it if the agent gets it wrong? If its… 1️⃣ Easy to undo, nobody notices: let it handle it (archiving newsletters, declining cold pitches) 2️⃣ Easy to undo, but it goes out in your name: have it draft and wait for your yes (client replies, anything that books your time) 3️⃣ Hard to undo: have it bring it straight to you (money, legal, anyone you know personally) As the drafts keep coming back good, things move up a bucket. Thanks again to Brian Sozzi and the Yahoo Finance team for having me. If you want the full clip, follow and comment YAHOO and I'll send it over."

@raydalio #43
Ray Dalio on Instagram: "Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle. Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble. So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle. #RayDalio #Economy #LongTermDebtCycle #Finance"

Dr. Rhonda Patrick on Instagram: "Bananas contain unusually high levels of polyphenol oxidase, or PPO, an enzyme responsible for browning that also degrades polyphenols. That’s why, on the occasion I happen to make a smoothie, I usually use a lower-PPO ingredient such as avocado instead. A high-PPO banana smoothie reduced peak blood levels of epicatechin-derived metabolites by 84% in a small, crossover experiment. A low-PPO mixed-berry smoothie preserved exposure. This was primarily a cocoa-epicatechin experiment rather than a direct test of blueberry anthocyanins or health outcomes. But PPO can oxidize epicatechin and blueberry chlorogenic acid, and the resulting compounds indirectly degrade anthocyanins. Bananas are healthy. But I think leaving them out of a food combination where they can interact too directly with polyphenols is a sensible optimization. This clip is from my new episode on the amazing benefits of blueberries. Available on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, and Spotify now!"

@markmanson #73
Mark Manson on Instagram: "In 2018, a team of psychologists at Harvard ran one of the simplest experiments I’ve ever read about, and I still think about it all the time. They sat people in front of a screen and showed them dots, one at a time. Some dots were blue. Some were purple. The job was easy. Look at the dot and say whether it’s blue. At first, everyone did fine. Then the researchers slowly cut back on the blue dots, and people started calling purple dots blue. Their brains were running low on blue, so they stretched the definition until they had enough of it again. The researchers didn’t stop at dots. They tried faces, and as the threatening faces got rarer, people started reading neutral faces as threatening. They tried research proposals, and as the unethical ones got rarer, perfectly harmless proposals started looking shady. They even warned some of the participants that this would happen. They offered others cash to stay consistent. The drift showed up anyway. The paper calls it “prevalence-induced concept change.” I call it the Blue Dot Effect, because nobody is going to remember “prevalence-induced concept change” at a dinner party. Now think about the biggest problem in your life five years ago. Maybe it was money. Maybe you were lonely, or stuck in a job that made you want to drive into a lake every Monday morning. There’s a decent chance you fixed it, or at least got a lot closer. And there’s a very good chance you don’t feel five years’ worth of better. A new problem moved into the spot the old one left. It’s probably smaller. It sure doesn’t feel smaller. That’s the blue dot. Your mind keeps a certain amount of worry on file, and when one worry leaves, it goes shopping for a replacement."

Dr. Rhonda Patrick on Instagram: "Regular blueberry intake has been linked to slower cognitive aging. Older women in the Nurses Health Study who ate at least half a cup of blueberries per week experienced slower cognitive decline than women who rarely ate them. The estimated difference was equivalent to being roughly 1.5 to 2.5 years younger cognitively. People who consume blueberries at least occasionally have been shown to experience a one-third lower risk of dementia than rare or non-consumers, and the highest blueberry consumption has been associated with up to a 50% lower risk. These studies are observational and cannot prove that blueberries prevent dementia. But alongside shorter randomized trials showing modest improvements in aspects of memory and cognition with blueberry intake, the long-term signal is intriguing. I discuss the brain benefits of blueberries and more in the latest episode of the podcast. Available now on YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts!"

Idris | Online Fitness Coach on Instagram: "One of the BEST Exercises for Your Obliques: half kneeling Pallof Press 🔥 Half Kneeling Pallof Press Anti Rotation Press Target muscles: Core, especially the obliques Equipment: Resistance band or cable machine Difficulty: Intermediate 1️⃣ Setup Kneel on one knee with the other foot positioned in front of you. Both knees should be at approximately 90°. Set the cable or resistance band around chest height. Hold it with both hands while positioning your body perpendicular to the anchor point. Keep your hips and chest facing forward and aligned. Keep your shoulders down without shrugging. Before you start, brace your core and maintain a neutral pelvis. 🎯 Goal: Create stability through the hips and spine and prevent your body from rotating against the resistance. 2️⃣ Press Hold your hands in front of your chest and press the handle straight forward with control. As you press, your torso, hips, and shoulders should not rotate toward the cable. Extend your arms only as far as you can while maintaining a stable body position. Exhale as you press. 🎯 Key point: The goal isn’t to rotate your torso; it’s to resist rotation. 3️⃣ Return Slowly bring your hands back toward your chest with control. Inhale as you return. Don’t let the band or cable pull your body toward the anchor point. Keep your hips and chest facing forward and stable. 🎯 Tip: Maintain core tension throughout the entire range of motion. 🎯 Benefits Improves core stability, pelvic control, and your ability to resist rotational forces. These qualities can help with force transfer during exercises such as squats, deadlifts, and other athletic movements. 📚 Source: American Council on Exercise (ACE Fitness) ⸻ #pallofpress #coretraining #obliquesworkout #gymtok #gymfam"

Idris | Online Fitness Coach on Instagram: "How to Do a Single-Arm Machine Chest Fly | Pec Deck Chest Fly Tutorial The machine used for this exercise is commonly called a Pec Deck or Machine Chest Fly. In this variation, you perform the movement one arm at a time to train each side of the chest independently. 🎯 Target Muscles: * Pectoralis Major * Anterior Deltoid ▶ Machine Setup Adjust the seat height so the machine handle is aligned with your chest and shoulder joint. Keep both feet flat on the floor to maintain stability throughout the movement. Keep your back and lower back against the pad, with your shoulders back and down. Grip the handle firmly with one hand. Keep the working elbow slightly bent and maintain a consistent elbow angle throughout the movement. Place your non-working hand on the other handle or a stable part of the machine to help maintain body stability. Choose a weight that allows you to perform the movement with full control without rotating your torso. ▶ How to Perform Keeping your body stable, move your working arm toward the midline of your body in a controlled motion. Exhale as you bring the handle forward and focus on contracting your chest. At the end of the movement, squeeze the chest under control without shrugging or moving your shoulder forward. Slowly return the handle to the starting position while inhaling. Do not allow your torso to rotate toward the working side. Keep your hips, lower back, and shoulders stable throughout the movement. Maintain a slight bend in the elbow and avoid turning the movement into a pressing motion. Do not allow the weight stack to fully rest between repetitions to maintain muscular tension. Complete your repetitions on one side, then repeat on the other side. Avoid using a weight that causes torso rotation, shoulder movement, or loss of control. 📚 Source: National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) #Chestfly #chestworkout #gymtok #gymfam #nycfitness"

But what if this fight was never really about keeping Starlink out? Here’s the contradiction I find fascinating: Jio and Airtel have both signed agreements to distribute Starlink in India, while also challenging aspects of the satellite spectrum framework. And that makes perfect business sense. Musk wants access to one of the world’s largest telecom markets. Jio wants to protect its existing network investments while building its own satellite business. Airtel has exposure to Starlink competitor Eutelsat OneWeb. And India has legitimate questions about security, spectrum pricing and control over critical communications infrastructure. The bigger prize isn’t necessarily satellite Wi-Fi for remote villages. It’s the possibility of satellites eventually connecting directly to ordinary smartphones, changing how telecom networks operate. Which raises a much more interesting question than whether Elon or Ambani is the villain: What if the smartest strategy isn’t stopping your competitor — but making sure you earn money even when your competitor wins? Because the future of Indian telecom may be less about towers versus satellites, and more about who controls the customer when both work together. Dr. Stacy T. Sims on Instagram: "Women respond differently to resistance training than men. We’re generally more fatigue-resistant, recover faster between sets, and often tolerate higher total training volumes. At the same time, gains in muscle mass can be slower, particularly if we're under-fueling, due to differences in muscle fiber behavior and anabolic signaling. Hormones matter, but not in the rigid way they’re sometimes presented online. Estrogen supports muscle repair, collagen synthesis, and neuromuscular coordination, which helps explain why some women may feel stronger or more powerful at certain times during their cycle. It also helps explain why we see a precipitous drop in power with an increase in soft tissue issues during perimenopause. However, responses are highly individual. Rather than prescribing training strictly by menstrual cycle phase (as we once used to), current best practice is to use individual symptoms, recovery, and performance feedback to guide when to push and when to pull back. Fixed calendar rules aren't supported by the evidence—and they're not how most women actually experience training. For peri- and postmenopausal women, declining estrogen makes resistance training even more important for maintaining muscle quality, strength, and bone density. Heavy and explosive loading—appropriately progressed and well-fueled—remains one of the most powerful tools we have for long-term health and function. ​Comment ESTROGEN to get the full article."

Keep your front knee aligned with your toes and avoid unwanted torso bending or rotation. ▶ STEP 3 — ASCENT AND NEXT STEP 10. Exhale and push through your front foot to return to an upright position. 11. Bring your rear leg forward and take a controlled step into the next repetition. 12. Maintain control of your shoulders, torso, and hips throughout the movement. Andrew Huberman, Ph.D. on Instagram: "SUCCESS IS DETERMINED BY HOW PRECISELY YOU MATCH YOUR GENUINE CURIOSITY TO THE WORK THAT YOU DO • Obviously, here I’m talking about career success (but there are parallels to this in other areas of life). Also obvious is that we can’t always do the work that we would like to do most. There are practical considerations. But ultimately, if we want to make a living doing what we love most and do our very best work, it’s important we invest time in what we are most interested in seeing in the world and curious about. This clip excerpt is from me as a guest on the podcast Invest With the Best. He asked me: “what is the kindest thing anyone has ever done for you?” My answer was that Barbara Chapman, who eventually became my PhD advisor, had reminded me that the most important thing is to work on the things we are most curious about. And ignore any internal or external noise about what we should be doing instead. Barbara and I went onto publish a lot of studies together. It was a ton of work, but we had so much fun doing those projects. In no small part because I was trying to answer the questions about the brain and brain development that were most burning for me at the time. Some years later, I shifted to working on other scientific questions (postdoc years) and then again (before tenure) and again (after tenure) and I eventually launched the Huberman Lab podcast. Because that’s where my curiosity went. Each stage worked out great. And there will be a next stage of interests at some point too. None of it came easy, but I’m so glad Barbara convinced me to follow my curiosity. Always. The takeaway is that whether field or career track is crowded or empty, if you follow your strongest curiosity, your motivation never flags (if you take care of yourself physically that is!) and you inevitably do your best work. So once again, while there are practical considerations along one’s life and career track, when you can, follow your curiosity, even if it means going against the grain. I did. And I never looked back. And I’ll continue to do that going forward. My wish for everyone - for you, is that you do the same."

You can live in India indefinitely, work and study here, and buy most types of property without applying for a new visa every time you enter the country. But there’s an important line many OCI holders misunderstand: OCI is not Indian citizenship. That means no voting rights, no contesting elections, no regular government jobs and restrictions still apply to purchasing agricultural land and farmland. So while an OCI card gives you significant rights to live and build a life in India, it doesn’t give you every right an Indian citizen has. The Anti-Doomscroll Briefing

Neutralizing the 10 Psychological Traps of Social Media

Mainstream short-form video algorithms are intentionally engineered as behavioral casinos—optimizing for time-on-screen rather than signal. Inspired by the educational breakdown in "The Brain Behind Your Phone Addiction. We Caught Him!" (Satvic Movement), Instagram Digest inverts this model:

1. Infinite Scrolling

Solved Replaced with a finite weekly batch and an explicit "You're All Caught Up! 🎉" milestone screen.

2. The Red Colour Trap

Solved Zero red badge counts or alarm dots. Replaced with quiet-luxury OLED slate tones and an optional 1-tap Grayscale Detox mode.

3. Gamified Friendship

Solved Completely severed social graph. Zero streaks, zero interaction scores, zero social obligation loops.

4. The Anticipation Trap

Solved Deterministic static compilation. Zero slot-machine pull-to-refresh roulette or delayed typing indicators.

5. Filtered Reality

Solved Whitelist ingestion targeting high-signal creators in science, tech, crafts, and finance, with lifestyle filters.

6. Customised Feed

Solved Replaces black-box recommendation neural nets with an open, fair-share algorithm capping creators at 4 reels.

7. Artificial Urgency

Solved Completely ignores 24h disappearing stories and live broadcasts. Asynchronous weekly briefing on your schedule.

8. Likes and Followers Count

Solved Completely strips like counts, view tallies, follower numbers, and public comment threads from the screen.

9. Simplicity (Hypnotic Trance)

Solved Introduces active decision friction: manual-advance option, 3-second breathers, and active session time-boxing.

10. The Buzz

Solved Zero real-time push notifications or vibration pings. 100% quiet, passive, on-demand pull model.
